options.contentEn: Increased business opportunities for top firms.

questions.stemEn: Compared with their predecessors, today's CEOs are required to ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。题干问与前任相比，当今CEO需要具备什么能力。第三段详述了当今CEO需具备的多项技能，核心论据之一是"large American companies are much more globalized than ever before, with supply chains spread across a larger number of countries"（美国大公司比以往更加全球化，供应链遍布更多国家），因此CEO需要"operate more globalized companies"（经营更全球化的公司）。选项D与此完全吻合。选项A的teamwork概念原文未突出强调；选项B的"finance more R&D"（资助更多研发）原文未提及；选项C"establish closer ties with tech companies"（与科技公司建立更紧密联系）与原文公司自身变成科技公司不同。

options.label: A
options.contentEn: foster a stronger sense of teamwork

options.label: C
options.contentEn: establish closer ties with tech companies

questions.stemEn: CEO pay has been rising since the 1970s despite ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。题干问自20世纪70年代以来，尽管存在什么因素，CEO薪酬仍持续上涨。第四段明确使用Yet构成转折："corporate governance has become a lot tighter and more rigorous since the 1970s. Yet it is principally during this period of stronger governance that CEO pay has been high and rising"（自70年代以来公司治理变得更加严格规范，然而正是在这一治理更加强化的时期CEO薪酬居高不下并持续上涨）。despite = Yet，即在严格公司治理存在的情况下薪酬仍上涨。选项B "strict corporate governance"准确对应原文。其他三个选项原文均未涉及。

questions.stemEn: High CEO pay can be justified by the fact that it helps ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。题干问CEO高薪可以因什么事实而得到辩护（justified）。末段末句明确指出"a sign that those practices build up corporate value not just for the CEO"（这些做法不仅为CEO而且为公司创造了价值），即高薪有助于"increase corporate value"（增加公司价值）。选项D与此完全吻合。选项A的"confirm the status of CEOs"（确认CEO地位）原文未着重讨论；选项B的"motive inside candidates"（激励内部候选人）与原文"highest CEO salaries are paid to outside candidates"最高薪付给外部候选人相矛盾；选项C的"boost the efficiency"（提高效率）原文讨论的是corporate value而非efficiency。

questions.stemEn: The most suitable title for this text would be ___.
questions.analysis: 主旨大意题。全文从多角度论证CEO高薪的合理性：首段承认CEO薪酬确实大幅上涨；第二段从商业机会与人才稀缺角度解释原因；第三段论述当今CEO所需技能远超以往；第四段反驳"剥削"观点，指出公司治理已更严格，高薪是为招聘顶尖人才；第五段指出最高薪付给外部候选人，且薪酬与股价挂钩能增加公司价值。整篇文章立场是为CEO高薪辩护，论证其合理性。选项A "CEOs Are Not Overpaid"（CEO并未薪酬过高）准确概括全文主旨。选项B"Past and Present"过于宽泛无立场；选项C聚焦CEO面临的挑战而忽略薪酬辩护核心；选项D聚焦CEO特质偏离主题。

options.label: D
options.contentEn: CEO Traits: Not Easy to Define

questions.stemEn: Which of the following is true about Madrid's clean air zone?
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。题干问关于马德里清洁空气区哪一项正确。第二段末句总结"But with legal battles ahead, the zone's future looks uncertain at best"（但由于前方还有法律纠纷，该区域的未来充其量看来是不确定的），即其命运尚待决定。选项D "Its fate is yet to be decided"是对此的准确概括。选项A的"Its effects are questionable"（效果存疑）与原文"despite its success in improving air quality"（尽管在改善空气质量方面取得了成功）相矛盾；选项B的"opposed by a judge"与原文法官overruled停止罚款的决定恰好相反——法官是支持恢复罚款的；选项C的"needs tougher enforcement"（需要更严厉执法），原文讨论的是执法被暂停而非需要加强。

options.label: B
options.contentEn: It has been opposed by a judge.

options.label: D
options.contentEn: Its fate is yet to be decided.

questions.stemEn: Which is considered a weakness of the city-level measures to tackle dirty air?
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。题干问城市层面应对污染空气的措施被认为存在什么弱点。第三段明确指出"they inevitably put the costs of cleaning the air on to individual drivers — who must pay fees or buy better vehicles — rather than on to the car manufacturers"（这些措施不可避免地将清洁空气的成本转嫁到个体驾驶者身上，而非转嫁给汽车制造商）。选项D "They put too much burden on individual motorists"中burden对应costs，individual motorists对应individual drivers。选项A的"biased against car manufacturers"与原文相反——措施偏袒的是汽车制造商而非消费者；选项B的"impractical for city councils"、选项C的"too mild for politicians"原文均未讨论。

options.label: A
options.contentEn: They are biased against car manufacturers.

options.label: B
options.contentEn: They prove impractical for city councils.

options.label: C
options.contentEn: They are deemed too mild for politicians.

options.label: D
options.contentEn: They put too much burden on individual motorists.

questions.stemEn: The author believes that the extension of London's Ulez will ___.
questions.analysis: 作者观点题。题干问作者认为伦敦超低排放区的扩展将产生什么结果。第四段明确预测"it is sure to spark intense opposition from the far larger number of motorists who will then be affected"（它必将引发强烈反对，因为届时受影响的驾驶者数量将大幅增加）。选项A "arouse strong resistance"中arouse = spark，strong resistance = intense opposition。选项B的"ensure Khan's electoral success"（确保Khan选举成功）与原文相反——这恰恰可能成为选举中的争议议题；选项C改善城市交通和选项D抑制汽车制造原文均未涉及。

questions.stemEn: Who does the author think should have addressed the problem?
questions.analysis: 作者观点题。题干问作者认为谁本应解决这一问题。第六段明确指出"They are acting because national governments — Britain's and others across Europe — have failed to do so"（地方官员之所以采取行动是因为各国政府未能做到），即解决问题本应属于国家政府的责任。should have addressed对应failed to do so——正是政府的失职才致使解决问题的主体缺失。选项D "National governments"直接对应原文。选项A的Local residents、选项B的Mayors、选项C的Councilors都是原文中已经在尽力而为但权责有限的主体，并非作者认为should have addressed（理应解决）的主体。

questions.stemEn: It can be inferred from the last paragraph that auto companies ___.
questions.analysis: 推理判断题。题干问从最后一段可以推断出汽车公司怎样。末段首句指出限制措施是"a response to the absence of a larger effort to properly enforce existing regulations and require auto companies to bring their vehicles into compliance"（对缺乏更大力度努力适当执行现有法规、要求汽车公司使其车辆合规的回应），末句更讽刺道"We're doing everything but insist that manufacturers clean up their cars"（我们想尽了一切办法，唯独坚持要求制造商整治他们的汽车），这暗示汽车公司应当被强制遵守法规。选项B "should be forced to follow regulations"准确表达了这一推断。选项A"will raise low-emission car production"原文未暗示企业会主动行动；选项C的"upgrade the design"过于具体化；选项D的"public supervision"（公众监督）偷换概念，原文关注的是政府监管而非公众监督。

options.label: B
options.contentEn: should be forced to follow regulations

options.label: C
options.contentEn: will upgrade the design of their vehicles

options.label: D
options.contentEn: should be put under public supervision

questions.stemEn: Generation Zs graduating college this spring ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。题干问今年春天毕业的Z世代怎样。首段明确提到"the attention has been rising steadily in recent weeks"（近几周来，对他们的关注度稳步上升）和"Everybody wants to know how the people who will soon inhabit those empty office cubicles will differ from those who came before them"（每个人都想知道他们将与前辈有何不同），说明Z世代正引起公众越来越多的关注。选项D "are drawing growing public attention" 中 drawing = has been rising，growing public attention = attention has been rising。选项A的"are recognized for their abilities"（能力被认可）、选项B的"optimistic about the labor market"（对劳动力市场乐观）、选项C的"in favor of office job offers"（偏爱办公室工作）原文均未涉及。

options.label: B
options.contentEn: are optimistic about the labor market

options.label: C
options.contentEn: are in favor of office job offers

questions.stemEn: Generation Zs are keenly aware ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。题干问Z世代清楚意识到什么。第二段明确指出"Gen Zs know what an economic train wreck looks like"（Z世代知道经济灾难是什么样子），并进一步解释他们在2008年金融危机期间亲眼目睹了父母失去工作和积蓄的经历。选项C "what a tough economic situation is like" 是对原文 know what an economic train wreck looks like 的同义改写，tough economic situation 对应 economic train wreck。选项A的"what their parents expect of them"（父母的期望）、选项B的"how valuable a counselor's advice is"、选项D的"how they differ from past generations"原文在此语境中均未涉及。

options.label: A
options.contentEn: what their parents expect of them

options.label: B
options.contentEn: how valuable a counselor's advice is

options.label: C
options.contentEn: what a tough economic situation is like

options.label: D
options.contentEn: how they differ from past generations

questions.stemEn: The word "assuage" (Line 9, Para. 2) is closest in meaning to ___.
questions.analysis: 词义猜测题。考查第二段中assuage一词的语义。原文"The booming economy seems to have done little to assuage this underlying generational sense of anxious urgency"（蓬勃发展的经济似乎对assuage这一代人内心深处的焦虑紧迫感效果甚微）。经济繁荣本应带来好处以减轻焦虑，但little to assuage表示几乎没有减轻，由此可推断assuage意为"缓解、减轻"。选项D "relieve"（缓解）与此一致。选项A "deepen"（加深）与文义相反——根据上下文，经济繁荣应带来正面缓解作用；选项B"define"（定义）和选项C"maintain"（维持）均不能与"anxious urgency"形成合理的动宾搭配。

questions.stemEn: It can be learned from Paragraph 3 that Generation Zs ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。题干问从第三段可以了解到Z世代的什么情况。第三段提供了两个调查数据：88%的应届毕业生选择专业时已考虑到就业；佐治亚大学就业指导中心发现学生最看重未来雇主提供稳定就业的能力。这充分说明Z世代"have a clear idea about their future job"（对自己未来的工作有清晰的想法）。选项B准确概括了这一核心观点。选项A中"give top priority to professional training"（将职业培训放在首位）与原文不符——原文中secure employment排第一，professional development and training排第二；选项C"care little about their job performance"（不太关心工作表现）原文未提及；选项D"think it hard to achieve work-life balance"曲解原文——原文只是将work-life balance列为第一目标，并未说难以实现。

options.label: A
options.contentEn: give top priority to professional training

options.label: B
options.contentEn: have a clear idea about their future job

options.label: C
options.contentEn: care little about their job performance

options.label: D
options.contentEn: think it hard to achieve work-life balance

questions.stemEn: Michelsen thinks that compared with millennials, Generation Zs are ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。题干问米克尔森认为与千禧一代相比，Z世代更加如何。末段中米克尔森指出"Millennials wanted more flexibility in their lives"（千禧一代希望生活中有更多灵活性），而"Generation Zs are looking for more certainty and stability"（Z世代追求更多确定性和稳定性），且"they are quite risk averse"（他们非常厌恶风险）。综合可知，与千禧一代相比，Z世代更不愿意冒险，更加谨慎求稳。选项B "less adventurous"（不那么喜欢冒险）准确概括了这一对比——adventurous的反面即是risk averse和seeking stability。选项A的"less realistic"（不那么现实）与原文"clear-eyed, economic pragmatists"（头脑清醒的经济实用主义者）矛盾；选项C的"more diligent"和选项D的"more generous"原文均未作比较。

questions.stemEn: Research by the World Economic Forum suggests ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。根据第一段定位至第三句，世界经济论坛的研究发现，到2022年，工作岗位中平均42%的"核心技能"将发生变化。这一研究支撑了前句提出的"热门工作岗位将迅速变化"的时势判断。末句"那是一个非常短的时间线"说明未来工作岗位迫切需要新的工作技能，[B]正确。[B]中demand for new job skills是对原文"core skills within job roles will change"和"the jobs in demand will change rapidly"的同义转述，urgent对应末句"a very short timeline"。选项[A]将原文a lot of would-be workers（潜在劳动者）曲解为全职就业岗位增加；[C]将原文the jobs in demand will change rapidly（热门工作迅速变化）曲解为job opportunities的稳步增长；[D]利用core skills编造存在争议，原文未提及对核心技能的不同意见。

options.label: B
options.contentEn: an urgent demand for new job skills

options.label: C
options.contentEn: a steady growth of job opportunities

questions.stemEn: AT&T is cited to show ___.
questions.analysis: 写作目的/例证题。第二段先指出个别公司面对技能不匹配时倾向于"解雇技能过时的员工，招聘具备所需技能的人"（即fire-and-hire策略），然后用"That does not always happen"转折引出AT&T的例子——该公司决定实施大规模再技能化项目而非采用fire-and-hire策略，被称为"典范"。因此，举AT&T的例子旨在说明存在替代fire-and-hire策略的方案，即[A]。[A]是对原文"decided to do a massive reskilling program rather than go with a fire-and-hire strategy"的准确概括。选项[B]利用本段后半部分government内容干扰，但AT&T是企业层面的案例而非政府层面；[C]将AT&T被誉为gold standard曲解为员工考核标准；[D]偏离主题，举例目的不是介绍再技能化项目的特征，而是说明存在不同于fire-and-hire的替代方案。

options.label: A
options.contentEn: an alternative to the fire-and-hire strategy

options.label: B
options.contentEn: an immediate need for government support

options.label: C
options.contentEn: the importance of staff appraisal standards

questions.stemEn: Efforts to resolve the skills mismatch in Canada ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。根据第二段末句，加拿大及其他地方为应对技能错配所做的努力"充其量可以说是迟缓的（languid at best）"，导致了即使在高失业率时期和地区也经常听到雇主迫切需要工人的矛盾局面。由此可知，加拿大的努力显然不充分，[D]正确。[D]中insufficient是对原文"languid at best"的同义转述，"appeared to be"对应原文"have been"。选项[A]将原文"employers begging for workers"暗示的劳动力短缺曲解为labor costs被推高；[B]将加拿大努力造成的矛盾局面（高失业率的同时雇主招不到人）偷换为"努力本身不一致"；[C]原文未提及遭遇激烈反对。

questions.stemEn: We can learn from Paragraph 3 that there was ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。第三段先指出疫情期间失业率高企，然后通过February（失业率低，工人短缺普遍）和May（失业率飙升，但并非所有短缺都消失了）的对比引出重点。最后以医疗领域为例明确指出"医生、护士和其他医务人员仍然明显短缺（clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel）"，[C]正确。选项[A]原文未提及政策调整的呼吁；[B]将原文的工人短缺现象变化曲解为"招聘实践的变化"；[D]与原文失业率飙升的描述完全相反。

questions.stemEn: Scandinavian Airlines decided to ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。根据题干关键词Scandinavian Airlines定位至末段第三句。该句指出，北欧航空公司决定启动一项短期再培训计划，"对下岗员工进行再技能化培训以支援医院工作人员"。即为其下岗员工转岗到其他工作做准备，[B]正确。[B]中prepare...for...对应原文reskilled...to...，other jobs指代hospital staff的工作。选项[A]将原文培训内部下岗员工支援外部缺人的单位曲解为"为失业者创造职位空缺"；[C]将培训对象"下岗客舱员工"偷换为"（在岗）客舱员工"，培训目的也由"支援医院"改为"提升服务"；[D]利用末句Swedish university编造"资助大学教育"，原文指的是瑞典大学参与了集体培训计划。

options.label: A
options.contentEn: create job vacancies for the unemployed

options.label: B
options.contentEn: prepare their laid-off workers for other jobs

options.label: C
options.contentEn: retrain their cabin staff for better services

questions.stemEn: Some people argue that food self-sufficiency in the UK would ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。根据第二段，一些人将英国脱欧视为扭转粮食进口趋势的机会，他们认为回归自给自足"would boost the farming industry, political sovereignty and even the nation's health"（将促进农业发展、加强政治主权甚至提升国民健康）。[B]中contribute to the nation's well-being是对boost the nation's health的同义转述。选项[A]利用第一段global population的预测数据干扰，该数据是全球层面的人口增长与粮食危机的关系，与英国无关；[C]将原文自给自足的益处之一（增强政治主权）曲解为"成为政府优先事项"；[D]将自给自足的益处（促进农业发展）反向曲解为对农业构成挑战。

options.label: A
options.contentEn: be hindered by its population growth

options.label: C
options.contentEn: become a priority of the government

options.label: D
options.contentEn: pose a challenge to its farming industry

questions.stemEn: The report by the University of Leeds shows that in the UK ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。根据第三段第一句，利兹大学关于英国食品生产的报告指出"85% of the country's total land area is associated with meat and dairy production"（英国国土总面积的85%与肉类和乳制品生产有关），[C]正确。[C]是对该句的概括改写：most land对应原文85 per cent，is used for对应is associated with。选项[A]、[B]、[D]均源自第四段内容（农场需更集约化、工厂式生产需要、绿色田野减少），这些是作者基于报告数据对未来措施的推测，并非报告本身显示的事实。

options.label: C
options.contentEn: most land is used for meat and dairy production

options.label: D
options.contentEn: more green fields will be converted for farming

questions.stemEn: Crop-growing in the UK is restricted due to ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。根据第五段，作者先指出"转向以植物为主的饮食也无济于事"，然后以"There is a good reason why"引出原因——英国之所以以畜牧业为主，是因为"其大部分地形的土壤或气候不适合在商业基础上种植农作物"。这说明英国农作物种植受限是自然条件所致，[C]正确。[C]中natural conditions是对原文"the right soil or climate"的准确概括。选项[A]中farming technology原文未提及；[B]将英国以畜牧业为主（饮食习惯以动物食品为主）倒果为因地解释为种植受限的原因，实际因果关系是自然条件导致无法种植→畜牧业为主→饮食习惯；[D]利用原文"on a commercial basis"编造商业利益因素，原文讨论的是"在商业规模基础上"种植的可行性而非商业利益阻碍。

questions.stemEn: It can be learned from the last paragraph that British people ___.
questions.analysis: 推断题。末段第一句指出英国目前消费的水果和蔬菜中"只有23%是本土种植的"（Just 23 per cent of the fruit and vegetables consumed in the UK are currently home-grown）。由此可反推，英国消费者食用的水果和蔬菜约77%依赖进口，即主要依靠进口来满足新鲜农产品需求，[A]正确。[A]中rely largely on imports是对原文"只有23%自产"的合理反向推断。选项[B]利用23%和30%的数字编造水果消费稳步增长；[C]将原文中"需要寻找空间来种植提供绝大部分卡路里摄入的谷物等作物"曲解为英国人在寻求减少卡路里摄入的措施；[D]将寻找空间种植谷物曲解为尝试种植新品种谷物。

options.label: A
options.contentEn: rely largely on imports for fresh produce

options.label: B
options.contentEn: enjoy a steady rise in fruit consumption

options.label: C
options.contentEn: are seeking effective ways to cut calorie intake

options.label: D
options.contentEn: are trying to grow new varieties of grains

questions.stemEn: The author's attitude to food self-sufficiency in the UK is ___.
questions.analysis: 态度题。全文作者围绕英国粮食自给自足的可行性展开讨论。第二段末句以设问句"but how feasible is this vision?"开启质疑；第三段以数据说明即使全国都建成畜牧场也无法满足肉类和乳制品需求；第四段指出实现自给需要大幅减少动物食品消费并采用工厂式生产，暗示代价巨大；第五段指出由于自然条件限制转向植物性饮食同样不可行；末段进一步指出即使采取最极端措施也只能满足30%的新鲜农产品需求。纵观全文，作者对英国粮食自给自足持怀疑态度，[B] doubtful正确。选项[A]defensive（辩护的）与全文质疑基调相反；[C]tolerant（容忍的）表示不反对但也不支持，与作者明确质疑立场不符；[D]optimistic（乐观的）与全文论证方向完全相反。

questions.stemEn: What is true about Wunderlist and Sunrise after their acquisitions?
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。根据第二段，两款应用后来都被废弃了（were later scrapped），但"它们的工程师团队留了下来（Their teams of engineers stayed on）"，使其成为大公司用来满足技术人才渴求的"人才收购"案例。由此可知，收购后工程师被保留，[A]正确。[A]中were retained对应原文stayed on。选项[B]原文未提及市值下降；[C]与原文"were later scrapped"和"used their best features"完全相反——技术功能被吸收后应用反而被废弃，并未改善；[D]原文未提及重新定价。

questions.stemEn: Microsoft's critics believe that the big tech companies tend to ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。根据第三段，微软的批评者认为Wunderlist和Sunrise的命运是大型科技公司"无情地吞噬任何挡路的创新型公司（chew up any innovative companies that lie in their path）"的例证。保罗·阿诺德抱怨说："They bought the seedlings and closed them down"（他们买下幼苗然后关掉），终结了可能变成竞争对手的企业。由此可见，批评者认为大科技公司倾向于消除潜在竞争对手，[B]正确。选项[A]原文未提及夸大产品质量；[C]将原文的合并收购与获取人才（acqui-hires）混淆为"不公平对待新技术人才"；[D]原文中"Microsoft declined to comment"并非忽视公众意见的证据。

questions.stemEn: Paul Arnold is concerned that small acquisitions might ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。根据第四段，保罗·阿诺德承认自己的业务依赖于将初创企业出售给大科技公司，但他对此心情复杂："But are they good for the American economy? I don't know."（但它们对美国经济有好处吗？我不知道。）这表明他担心小型收购可能损害国家经济，[C]正确。[C]是对原文"good for the American economy"这一担忧的同义转述。选项[A]与原文语境完全相反——阿诺德担心的是收购对整体经济的影响，而非削弱大公司；[B]与原文相反——批评者认为收购消除了竞争而非恶化了竞争；[D]原文明确指出阿诺德自身的业务依赖于此类收购，他并非担心收购会打击投资者。

questions.stemEn: The US Federal Trade Commission intends to ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。根据第五段，美国联邦贸易委员会表示想找到上述问题的答案（即小型收购对美国经济是否有利），并要求五家最有价值的美国科技公司提供过去十年诸多小规模收购的信息。虽然现阶段仅是一个研究项目，但这已"引发了监管机构涉足早期科技市场的前景"。由此可知，FTC意图审查小型收购，[C]正确。[C]中examine对应原文"asked...for information about their many small acquisitions"。选项[A]将审查信息曲解为限制大科技公司扩张，程度过重且原文未提；[B]原文未提及鼓励研究合作；[D]将审查大公司的收购行为曲解为监管初创企业的运营，对象错位。

questions.stemEn: For the five biggest tech companies, their small acquisitions have ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。根据第六段，五大科技公司过去五年每年在10亿美元以下收购上的平均支出仅为34亿美元，与其庞大的财务储备及去年在美国投资的逾1300亿美元风险资本相比"a drop in the ocean"（沧海一粟）。由此可知，这些小型收购几乎没有给大公司带来财务压力，[A]正确。[A]是对原文"only $3.4 billion a year"和"a drop in the ocean compared with their massive financial reserves"的准确概括。选项[B]将财务压力替换为管理挑战，原文未提及管理问题；[C]利用examples、in their path等词汇拼凑，原文意在批评而非树立榜样；[D]原文未提及小型收购产生了可观的利润。

options.label: C
options.contentEn: set an example for future deals

questions.stemEn: Nalini Ambady's study deals with ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。根据第一段，安巴迪的研究被称为"thin slicing"（薄片撷取），即通过极少信息进行快速判断的能力。该研究与第一段首句相呼应：我们擅长基于"first impressions"（第一印象）来判断他人。研究结果表明，参与者通过观看10秒视频对教授的评分与学生期末评分高度相关，即使同时进行倒数计数占用工作记忆，评分同样准确。这证明了第一印象的可靠性，[B]正确。[B]中the reliability of first impressions是对全文核心主题的准确概括。选项[A]利用原文"occupying their conscious working memory"断章取义——该操作的目的是排除思考干扰而非测试记忆力；[C]利用原文professors、instructor和students等词汇拼凑，研究的核心是第一印象的准确性而非师生互动本身；[D]原文未讨论人们影响他人的能力。

questions.stemEn: In Ambady's study, rating accuracy dropped when participants ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。根据第二段，当另一组参与者在评分前被要求花一分钟写下判断理由（即进行深思熟虑）时，准确率急剧下降。安巴迪推测，深思熟虑使参与者将注意力集中在"vivid but misleading cues"（生动但具有误导性的线索）上，如某些手势或话语，而不是让微妙信号形成整体印象。由此可知，当参与者专注于具体细节时评分准确率下降，[A]正确。[A]是对原文"deliberation focused them on vivid but misleading cues"的同义转述。选项[B]将原文"spend a minute"曲解为有限时间造成了压力——实际上时间限制本身并非准确率下降的原因，而是写理由引发的深思熟虑行为；[C]利用10-second和15-second clips编造视频时长与准确率的关系；[D]原文未涉及参与者之间的讨论。

options.label: B
options.contentEn: gave the rating in limited time

questions.stemEn: Judith Hall mentions driving to show that ___.
questions.analysis: 写作目的/例证题。朱迪斯·霍尔的驾驶类比出现在第三段，其核心观点是：就像开手动挡汽车一样，"如果你开始想得太多，你就记不得自己在做什么。但如果你靠自动导航（凭直觉），你就没问题。"该类比旨在支持前句的研究发现——我们依赖直觉而非反思时更善于从薄片信息中察觉欺骗。换言之，反思/深思熟虑可能分散注意力、造成干扰，[A]正确。[A]中reflection can be distracting是对霍尔观点的准确概括。选项[B]利用原文"can't remember"断章取义，并非讨论记忆的选择性；[C]将社交生活的比喻曲解为"社交技能需要培养"；[D]与原文"better at detecting deception...when we rely on intuition"相反——原文指出直觉比反思更能察觉欺骗，并非欺骗难以察觉。

questions.stemEn: When you are making complex decisions, it is advisable to ___.
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。根据第四段末句，人们做出的购车决策"both objectively better and more personally satisfying when asked to focus on their feelings rather than on details, but only if the decision was complex"（当被要求专注于感受而非细节时，既在客观上更优，在个人满意度上也更高，但仅当决策复杂时如此）。由此可知，在做复杂决策时，专注于感受（即听从直觉）是可取的，[D]正确。[D]中follow your feelings是对原文"focus on their feelings"的同义转述。选项[A]与原文"focus on feelings rather than on details"相反——原文建议关注感受而非收集数据；[B]与原文"weren't asked to analyze their rationale"（不要求分析理由）相反——列举偏好正是分析理由的一种形式；[C]与原文"ratings aligned better with experts' opinions when the students weren't asked to analyze"逻辑不符——不需要分析时反而更接近专家意见，并非建议寻求专家意见。

questions.stemEn: What can we learn from the last paragraph?
questions.analysis: 事实细节题。末段指出直觉的特殊力量只在特定情况下释放，并介绍了一项研究：参与者完成八项任务，四项涉及反思性思维（辨别规则、理解词汇），四项涉及直觉和创造力（创造新产品或修辞手法）。结果表明"Use of their gut hurt their performance on the first four tasks"（使用直觉损害了前四项反思性任务的表现），但同时有助于后四项创造性任务。这说明直觉可能影响反思性任务（产生负面效果），[B]正确。[B]是对原文"Use of their gut hurt their performance on the first four tasks"的准确概括——gut对应Intuition，the first four tasks即reflective tasks。选项[A]利用原文"generating new products"断章取义，将其从任务类型的举例偷换为结论；[C]将原文"comprehending vocabulary"（理解词汇，属于反思性任务）与"creativity"（创造力，属于不同类型）强行关联——原文明确将二者分属不同任务类型；[D]与原文语境完全相反——原文强调的是直觉的应用场景，而非客观思维能提升直觉能力。

questions.stemEn: The climate-friendly eggs are produced ___.
questions.analysis: 细节题。第一段指出This all seems random, but it's by design（看似随意，实则精心设计），对应选项D on specially designed farms。选项A的low cost未提及；选项B regular shoppers未提及；选项C将气候友好型鸡蛋视为有机鸡蛋的替代品，而原文说它们still labeled organic，并非替代品。

options.label: B
options.contentEn: at the demand of regular shoppers

options.label: C
options.contentEn: as a replacement for organic eggs

questions.stemEn: Larry Brown is excited about his progress in ___.
questions.analysis: 细节题。第三段Brown描述了他的进展：增加覆盖作物→吸引虫子供鸡吃→鸡粪肥田→母鸡觅食高质量天然饲料→对土地、母鸡、鸡蛋都有好处。这是一个完整的可持续循环系统，对应选项C creating a sustainable system。选项A与原文draw worms（吸引虫子）相反；选项B disposal原文未提；选项D attracting customers非重点。

questions.stemEn: The example of organic eggs is used in Paragraph 4 to suggest ___.
questions.analysis: 细节题。第四段以有机鸡蛋为例：从被贬为小众产品到在沃尔玛出售，说明它成功了。后面提到如果可持续鸡蛋推广成功，将为再生牛肉等打开闸门。因此有机鸡蛋的例子暗示了再生产品的潜力。

options.label: B
options.contentEn: the setbacks in the egg industry

questions.stemEn: It can be learned from the last paragraph that young people ___.
questions.analysis: 推断题。最后一段指出younger generations are more concerned about climate change, shoppers wanting to signal their desire to protect the environment, Young adults really care about the planet。由此可推断，年轻人更可能购买气候友好型鸡蛋。

options.label: A
options.contentEn: are reluctant to change their diet

options.label: B
options.contentEn: are likely to buy climate-friendly eggs

questions.stemEn: John Brunnquell would disagree with Julie Stanton over regenerative products' ___.
questions.analysis: 细节题。Julie Stanton认为再生产品a hard sell（难推销），而John Brunnquell则认为the same consumers will embrace sustainability，年轻人really care about the planet。两人在再生产品的市场前景上有分歧。选项B nutritional value是Stanton提到though some producers say their eggs have more protein，但不是Brunnquell的观点分歧点；选项C standard definition只有Stanton提到；选项D moral implication未涉及。

questions.stemEn: The survey conducted by Harris Poll indicates that ___.
questions.analysis: 细节题。第一段第一句即为全文主旨：More Americans are opting to work well into retirement。调查数据也支持这一点：One in three Americans have or plan to have a job in retirement。选项D more Americans are willing to work in retirement是对文章主旨的同义转述。选项A physically fit错误，原文是mentally fit；选项B比较级原文未提及；选项C与原文相反。

options.label: A
options.contentEn: over half of the retirees are physically fit for work

options.label: B
options.contentEn: the old workforce is as active as the younger one

options.label: C
options.contentEn: one in three Americans enjoy earlier retirement

options.label: D
options.contentEn: more Americans are willing to work in retirement

questions.stemEn: It can be inferred from Paragraph 3 that Americans tend to think that ___.
questions.analysis: 推断题。第三段指出不退休的原因除了经济需求外，还包括staying mentally fit, preventing boredom or avoiding depression（保持心理健康、防止无聊、避免抑郁）。由此可推断，美国人认为退休可能导致这些问题，即退休可能给他们带来问题。选项A正确。选项B与原文相反（boredom是退休后的问题而非被缓解）；选项C原文未提overlooked；选项D economy未提及。

options.label: A
options.contentEn: retirement may cause problems for them

options.label: B
options.contentEn: boredom can be relieved after retirement

options.label: C
options.contentEn: the mental health of retirees is overlooked

questions.stemEn: Retirement patterns are changing partly due to ___.
questions.analysis: 细节题。第五段第一句明确给出原因：One reason for the change in retirement patterns: Americans are living longer。选项C longer life expectancy是living longer的同义替换。

questions.stemEn: Many retires are increasing in savings by ___.
questions.analysis: 细节题。第六段最后一句：Among the most popular ways they are doing this is by reducing their overall expenses。reducing their overall expenses = spending less。注意原文题干为unretirees而非retirees，选项D spending less是reducing expenses的同义替换。

questions.stemEn: With regard to retirement, Brent Weiss thinks that many people are ___.
questions.analysis: 细节题。第七段Brent Weiss指出：many people are worried about making ends meet，建议preretirees去找financial adviser设定长期目标。第八段又说Many people believe they can't retire。综合可见许多人没有做好准备，即unprepared。选项B、D与worried/can't retire矛盾；选项C失望文中未提。

questions.stemEn: It can be learned from the first two paragraphs that dark patterns ___.
questions.analysis: 细节题。第二段第一句定义了dark patterns为manipulate user interfaces to influence the decision-making ability of users（操纵用户界面以影响用户决策能力）。选项C undermine users' decision-making是influence the decision-making ability的同义替换，undermine与impair同义。选项A与原文内容相反；选项B leak information未提及；选项D remind与原文manipulate方向相反。

questions.stemEn: The 2019 study on dark patterns is mentioned to show ___.
questions.analysis: 细节题。第三段引用2019年研究的数据：about one in 10 employs these design practices（十分之一采用暗黑模式），紧接着说Though widely prevalent（尽管广泛存在）。该研究目的是通过数据show暗黑模式的广泛存在/strong presence。选项D正确。选项A major flaws和C severe damage均未提及；选项B complex designs非此段重点。

questions.stemEn: To handle digital deception, businesses should ___.
questions.analysis: 细节题。第四段明确给出企业应对digital deception的方法：Businesses should engage in conversations with IT, compliance, risk, and legal teams and include in the discussion...。engage in conversations with these teams = talk with relevant teams。选项B正确。

questions.stemEn: The additional regulations under the CCPA are intended to ___.
questions.analysis: 细节题。第五段明确说明：The regulations aim to ban dark patterns—ensures that consumers will not be confused or misled。选项B protect consumers from being tricked是not be confused or misled的同义替换。

questions.stemEn: According to the last paragraph, a key to coping with dark patterns is ___.
questions.analysis: 细节题。最后一段指出：Dark patterns also can be addressed on a self-regulatory basis, but only if organizations hold themselves accountable。self-regulatory（自律）和hold themselves accountable（对自己负责）均指向企业的自律。选项B businesses' self-discipline是self-regulatory的同义替换。

questions.stemEn: Scientists generally believe that the effects of ethics classes are ___.
questions.analysis: 细节题。第一段第一句：scientists are unsure if their lessons can actually change behavior; evidence either way is weak。unsure和evidence weak说明效果难以确定。选项A hard to determine是对unsure和weak evidence的准确概括。

questions.stemEn: Which of the following is a reason for the researchers to study meat-eating?
questions.analysis: 细节题。第二段第二句给出三个reason：students' attitudes are variable and unstable, behavior is easily measurable, and ethics literature largely agrees that eating less meat is good。选项B It is a behavior easy to measure对应第二个原因：behavior is easily measurable。选项A原文未提common；选项C student health未提及；选项D hot topic未提。

options.label: B
options.contentEn: It is a behavior easy to measure.

options.label: C
options.contentEn: It is important to students' health.

options.label: D
options.contentEn: It is a hot topic in ethics classes.

questions.stemEn: Eric Schwitzgebel's previous findings suggest that ethics professors ___.
questions.analysis: 细节题。第三段第一句指出：ethics professors do not differ from other professors on a range of behaviors, including voting rates, blood donation and returning library books。伦理学教授在行为上与其他教授无区别，这意味着伦理学教授并不必然在道德上更好。选项D are not necessarily ethically better符合。选项A、B、C均为未提及的无端推测。

options.label: A
options.contentEn: are seldom critical of their students

options.label: B
options.contentEn: are less sociable than other professors

options.label: C
options.contentEn: are not sensitive to political issues

questions.stemEn: Nina Strohminger thinks that the effect of the intervention is ___.
questions.analysis: 细节题。第四段Nina Strohminger说：wants the effect to be real but cannot rule out some unknown confounding variable（希望效果真实但不能排除未知混淆变量）。and if real, it might be reversible（即使真实也可逆转）。她的态度是不确定的。选项C uncertain正确。
